about.title: Hollister Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing a family member in a preventable collision changes everything, and the legal side of that loss can feel like one more burden on top of grief. In Hollister, where local roads such as 4th Street, San Benito Street, San Felipe Road and Rt 25 see steady weekend traffic, families are sometimes left facing a wrongful death claim with no idea where to start. California law limits who may bring this type of claim, usually a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, with other dependents eligible in certain situations, and there is a strict two-year window from the date of death to act, shorter still if a government entity may be involved. We handle wrongful death claims on a contingency basis, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is obtained. Our team can evaluate the circumstances, explain your options, and guide you through the process.

items.title: Standing Matters, and It's Limited
items.desc: California restricts who can file a wrongful death claim, typically a spouse, domestic partner, or children first, then other dependents or heirs. We can confirm who in your family qualifies and guide the process from there.

items.title: The Two-Year Clock Is Firm
items.desc: California generally gives families two years from the date of death to file, and that window shrinks considerably if a government entity is involved. Getting started early gives us more time to build your case properly.

items.title: No Upfront Cost During a Hard Time
items.desc: We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover compensation for your family. That means you're not paying legal bills while also grieving a loss.

items.question: Who is allowed to file a wrongful death claim in California?
items.answer: Generally, a surviving spouse, domestic partner, or children have the first right to file. If none exist, other dependents or heirs may be eligible under California law. We can review your family's specific situation to confirm eligibility.

items.question: How long do we have to file after a fatal crash in Hollister?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of death to bring a wrongful death claim, though that deadline is much shorter if a government agency, like a county road authority, may share responsibility. Given that many Hollister crashes occur on corridors such as San Felipe Road or Rt 25, which involve public infrastructure, it's worth getting a timeline reviewed quickly. Waiting too long can limit your options.

items.question: What kinds of compensation can a wrongful death claim cover?
items.answer: Recoverable losses can include funeral and burial costs, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. Every family's losses look different, and we can walk through what applies to your situation. This is a civil claim, separate from any criminal case that may also be pending.

items.question: Is there any cost to speak with us about your wrongful death claim?
items.answer: No. There's no cost for a consultation, and there's no obligation to move forward. We work on contingency, so there's no fee unless we recover compensation for your family.
